thread:
ashok: Heads up — after last night's kernel + driver churn we saw ~6% of GPU hosts in us-west-2 fail NVidia init (several hosts not binding nvidia-modeset). Affected nodes moved to degraded and some pods OOMed during init. Opening thread to coordinate an emergency holdlist and hotfix plan. INC-2026-0421

devon: saw the alerts from infra-telemetry. A few runner jobs hit CrashLoop on startup complaining about libnvidia-ml.so missing / driver mismatch. Noticed hosts that upgraded kernel 6.1.x are the ones failing. cc @julia :eyes:

julia: confirmed — we pushed a partial kernel slip last night for perf tests and it looks like some drivers (535.* vs 536.*) behave badly with our current kernel build. Reboot -> rollback to previous kernel fixes a tested host. I can produce a small repro log.

kai: we should do three things immediately: 1) create package hold/pinning for the GPU fleets in affected regions, 2) roll back driver where newer driver was installed, 3) freeze AMI bakes that include the new kernel/driver until we define a compatibility matrix. Suggest a lockstep matrix mapping kernel version -> driver build -> cuDNN tag per instance family.

ashok: (typo, corrected) ashok: Proposed immediate action plan: 
- apply apt-mark/yum versionlock hold on kernel packages + nvidia-driver on all GPU nodes in us-west-2 and eu-west-1
- patch the bootstrap to force driver=535.86-1 where nodes already upgraded to 536.x and failing
- run a controlled rollback for nodes showing NVRM errors, one AZ at a time
- create canary preflight that checks nvidia-smi + basic ml-serving smoke before marking node healthy

devon: add cost/impact note — holding older drivers means we miss perf improvements from 536+. On our rough calc, token-latency perf wins translate to ~3-8% infra savings, but the availability risk is higher. If holdlist lasts 2 weeks, estimate conservative $3k/week lost-opportunity cost (not infra overspend). I think that's acceptable to buy stability.

julia: I'll open a PR to infra-playbooks with the rollback and hold steps. Quick runbook snippet: 
```bash
# hold kernel + driver on deb/rpm hosts
sudo apt-mark hold 'linux-image-6.1*' || true
sudo apt-mark hold 'nvidia-driver-*' || true
# yum variant
sudo yum versionlock add nvidia-driver-535* || true
```
I'll also attach the repro logs to INC-2026-0421 and the bootstrap patch.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421 created by ashok in channel eng-infra. Priority: P2. Pager duty: infra-oncall. Related alerts: GPU_INIT_FAIL_USW2 (47 hosts), NODE_DEGRADED (12 hosts).

kai: we need an automated version gate in infra-config that refuses AMI / bootstrap with kernel+driver combos not on our approved matrix. I'll sketch a schema: 
- matrix entries: {hw_family, kernel_version, nvidia_driver, cudnn, validated_images:[ami-ids]}
- canary job will run `nvidia-smi && python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.device_count())"` as a quick smoke
I'll also add a feature flag to opt-in per region so we can lift hold faster in low-risk zones.

ops-bot: FYI: started a rolling rollback job for us-west-2 GPU pool (job id: rollback-1801023345-01). Started AZ-a. ETA per host ~10m.

ashok: sequencing note — do NOT run mass reboots. Rollback hosts individually and validate smoke. Keep one AZ as a control. Ops-oncall to coordinate window tonight 02:00-04:00 UTC.

devon: Also check NCCL versions on container images; we've seen NCCL ABI mismatches when kernel-driver combos change. If we pin drivers, we should ensure the container runtime isn't forcing incompatible NCCL libs.

julia: good point. I'll bake a quick check into the canary: compare /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnccl.so.* with container libnccl and fail early.

kai: long term: we should maintain a matrix doc in repo + automated CI that validates new kernels/drivers on a fleet-shaped hardware simulator (small cluster) before rolling. For now, I'll add a preflight policy to block image promotion if the combo isn't in matrix.

ashok: TL;DR: immediate holds in two regions, targeted rollbacks (AZ-by-AZ), add canary preflight + matrix, and create a temporary version gate for AMI promotion. Ops oncall to run the rollback tonight. Julia/kai/devon to own playbook + infra-config PRs. :thumbsup:

julia: PRs opened: infra/playbooks#392 (rollback), infra/config#128 (version gate). Attaching logs to the incident.

devon: 👍 will monitor telemetry and update INC-2026-0421 with numbers.

kai: I'll write the initial matrix doc and a minimal automation to enforce it. Pushing to infra-config in the next 2 hours.

ashok: Thanks all — keep updates in this thread and on the incident.
